title: Bloom + age-segmentation KV allocator with lane compaction for reduced fragmentation
creator: Samira O'Neill
description: Goal: implement a low-overhead KV allocation strategy that reduces long-term fragmentation on GPUs while cooperating with continuous batching. We will introduce a bloom-filtered age-segmentation suballocator (BFAS) plus a lightweight lane compaction process that runs opportunistically during low-load windows. Key constraints: <=2% steady-state GC CPU overhead, no p99 latency regression for generation requests, and <5% additional memory reserved for metadata.
background: Existing allocators suffer from slow-growing micro-fragmentation driven by interleaved KV lifetimes and multi-tenant continuous batching patterns. Prior tickets focused on slab and buddy heuristics; those approaches improved worst-case but left residual fragmentation when allocation footprints are heterogeneous and temporal locality is weak. Continuous batching amplifies cross-request memory churn because batched KV slots are populated with many short-lived tokens followed by bursts of long-lived prefixes.
proposal: We propose BFAS: allocate GPU KV pools split into age buckets (hot, warm, cold) with each bucket further subdivided into small lanes. Each incoming allocation is fingerprinted (fast 32-bit hash of request+model+prefix-length) and placed into a lane chosen by a bloom filter+age heuristic to maximize affinity with similar allocations. The bloom filter tracks recent occupancy patterns per lane (cheap bitset update) so the allocator prefers neighboring free slots to co-locate likely-to-live-together entries, reducing scattering. When fragmentation score for a pool exceeds a threshold (measured by sampled free-run histograms), a non-blocking lane compaction agent migrates live entries from sparse lanes to denser lanes in the same age bucket using GPU memcpy and KV index updates. Compaction is gated by load and batch scheduler signals: it yields when tail-latency approaches SLOs or when active batch size exceeds a threshold. We will integrate allocator hints into the continuous batcher so batches prefer allocations that keep hot/warm locality intact.
design_decisions: 1) Use bloom filter (8-16 bytes per lane) instead of per-token metadata to reduce metadata overhead. 2) Age buckets are time-decayed (exponential decay window) to avoid manual reclassification. 3) Lane compaction runs cooperatively with scheduler and uses incremental evacuation (copy a small set of items per compaction tick) to bound p99 impact. 4) Maintain a compact relocation map stored in GPU-visible pinned memory so index updates are asynchronous and consistent across kernels. 5) Fall back to existing slab allocator when compaction is disabled or when migration fails.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 2w): implement BFAS allocator prototype in dev runtime; expose bloom lanes and lane chooser. Phase 2 (integration, 3w): integrate with continuous batcher and instrument allocation telemetry (histograms, lane occupancy, bloom false-positive rate). Phase 3 (compaction, 2w): implement lane compaction agent with cooperative yield hooks to scheduler. Phase 4 (canary, 2w): rollout to canary hosts with telemetry dashboards and kill-switch config. Phase 5 (gradual rollout, 2w): expand to >50% traffic, monitor fragmentation metric and latency SLOs. Each phase includes unit tests and microbench harness for GPU memcpy/migration timing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fragmentation score (sampled free-run histogram kurtosis) improves by >=35% vs baseline under mixed short/long KV workload.
- No regression in generation p99 latency >5% on canary hosts.
- Compaction CPU overhead <=2% of host CPU and memory metadata <=5% of KV pool.
- Telemetry dashboards emit lane occupancy, compaction throughput, bloom FP rate, and migration latency.
- Feature controlled by runtime flags and has immediate kill-switch to disable compaction or BFAS.
risks:
- Bloom filter FP could co-locate unrelated items and worsen fragmentation in some patterns. Mitigation: tune bloom width and fall back to random lane.
- Migration cost might spike under certain GPU memory pressure patterns; compaction is rate-limited and load-aware.
- Integration bugs in index relocation may cause transient cache misses; implement thorough consistency checks and canary-only rollout first.
- Telemetry noise might mask true fragmentation; add synthetic workloads to validate metrics.
testing_and_telemetry:
- Microbench harness that reproduces mixed lifetime workload (70% short 1-10 steps, 30% long 500+ steps) and measures allocator fragmentation curve.
- End-to-end canary tests with production-like batch interleaving and token distributions.
- Dashboards: lane-occupancy heatmap, bloom FP rate over time, compaction bytes/sec, migration latency distribution, free-run histogram and derived fragmentation score.
- Alerting: fragmentation score drift >20% or compaction migration latency > 2x baseline triggers pager and automatic compaction backoff.
notes: This approach leans on probabilistic grouping (bloom) and temporal age-bucketing to reduce overhead vs heavy-weight per-token metadata approaches. It is intended to complement, not replace, existing slab and buddy strategies; we will add BFAS as an alternate suballocator and test mixed-mode operation. If successful, BFAS could also inform routing decisions at the smart router level to reduce cross-model contamination.
